question: What was the name of the bilateral naval exercise held between India and Russia in the Bay of Bengal and Chennai from 28 March to 2 April 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**INDRA**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **INDRA** is a bilateral naval exercise conducted between **India** and **Russia**. It is aimed at improving operational interoperability and enhancing maritime cooperation between the two nations.
 
• The **2025 edition of INDRA** was held in the **Bay of Bengal** and **Chennai** from **28 March to 2 April**, demonstrating joint efforts in maritime security.
 
• The exercise included various activities such as **anti-piracy operations**, **search and rescue missions**, and advanced naval drills to strengthen the maritime partnership between India and Russia.
 
• INDRA serves as a platform for both nations to exchange **military expertise**, conduct **tactical exercises**, and foster mutual trust and understanding.
 
• The exercise also highlights the shared commitment of India and Russia towards ensuring **regional and global maritime security**.
 
• The participation of advanced naval assets and personnel from both sides reflects the strategic importance of the exercise in strengthening defense ties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India-Russia Defense Cooperation:**

 
 
• India and Russia share a **long-standing strategic partnership** in defense, with multiple agreements focusing on technology transfer, joint production, and military exercises.
 
• INDRA exercises are part of this collaboration, showcasing the growing defense ties between the two nations.
 
 
 
• **Previous Exercises:**
 
 
• INDRA was first conducted in **2003** and has evolved over the years to include **tri-service engagements**, covering land, air, and sea domains.
 
• The exercise is held alternately in Indian and Russian territories, emphasizing the importance of shared responsibilities in maritime security.
 
 
 
• **Other Naval Exercises of India:**
 
 
• **VARUNA:** A bilateral exercise between **India and France**, focusing on enhancing interoperability and conducting advanced naval drills.
 
• **SHAKTI:** A military exercise between **India and France**, primarily focusing on ground forces.
 
• **BRAHMOS:** Although not a naval exercise, it refers to the **joint development of the BrahMos missile** between India and Russia.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of INDRA:**

 
 
• INDRA strengthens the **maritime partnership** between India and Russia and reflects their shared commitment to security in the Indian Ocean region.
 
• It helps both nations to **develop strategies** to counter common challenges such as piracy, terrorism, and maritime threats.
 
 
 
• **Regional Importance:**
 
 
• The Bay of Bengal is a **strategically important region**, serving as a major trade route and a hub for maritime activities.
 
• The presence of naval forces from India and Russia in this region helps ensure the safety and security of international shipping lanes.
